messages:
maya: Heads up — we just got a pile of IOPS saturation alerts in eu-west2, GPUs queuing and batch jobs failing fast. Several nodes hit >95% avg iops util. dmesg shows write stalls and blk_update_request errors.

infra-bot: [ALERT] iops_saturation on gnode-4234,gnode-4270,gnode-4301 — 50 nodes affected. threshold=90%. see: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/alerts/2468246812

arjun: I saw this spike. Looks like the ephemeral-cleaner ran across many hosts right after the midnight AMI rollout. Cleaner overlap = fanout of heavy scrubs + GC.

sofia: iostat snapshot from gnode-4234 at 02:13:01 UTC:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1.20  302.40  24.00 6144.00  25.12   0.72  99.98
```
latencies are through the roof.

jessica: Any kernel scrub or fsck running? Could be large file deletions causing heavy writes (metadata storms).

maya: Confirmed — cleaner logs show massive concurrent deletes (tmp shards + model caches). Also a few nodes logged: `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456` — need to watch for corruption.

lee: Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle cleaner parallelism in eu-west2, 2) temporarily route new batch provisioning to us-west, 3) bump node drain grace and reduce batch pod burst to limit write amplification. Which do we want first?

marco: Cost/health note: write amplification here will accelerate NVMe wear. Projecting ~1.8x writes for this week if it keeps up — that reduces expected lifetime for the local class. We should throttle now to avoid replacements.

arjun: Agree with lee. Also add jitter to cleaner controller so it doesn't align with AMI rollout. We should treat cleaner as a low-priority background job with rate limits.

sofia: I'm going to patch the cleaner in eu-west2 to `--parallelism=2` and add `--delete-rate=1000` for now. Command: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch deployment/ephemeral-cleaner -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"cleaner","args":["--parallelism=2","--delete-rate=1000"]}]}}}}'
```
Applying now.

maya: Also rolling a temporary admission controller tweak to deny large ephemeral writes from batch pods (limit to 8GB) until we see stable iops.

sofia: Patch applied. Watching metrics.

infra-bot: [INFO] cleaner pods restarted (eu-west2) — 12/12 ready.

~10m later~

maya: Update — iops util dropped to ~35% across the previously affected nodes, queue depth normalized, no new blk_update_request errors since patch. GPU provisioning queue cleared.

marco: Good. Let's add a follow-up: 1) schedule cleaner rollout stagger for future AMI pushes, 2) add NVMe write-rate alert that correlates with cleaner events, 3) run lifecycle projection for affected node class.

jessica: I'll open a postmortem doc with the timeline and attach logs.

arjun: For long-term: consider implementing per-host KV-cache eviction delay and stronger writeback batching in the cleaner to reduce random writes. Also evaluate increasing ephemeral disk size for batch nodes to reduce forced rapid deletes.

maya: Thanks all. Marking alert as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: [RESOLVED] iops_saturation on eu-west2 cleared (2468246812)

sofia: :thumbsup: will follow up with graphs and the exact patch diff in the postmortem.
